passages.title: Rising Star: An Interview with Leo Vance
passages.text:
At just sixteen, Leo Vance has already made a name for himself in the world of competitive swimming. We caught up with him at his local training centre in Manchester. 'I started swimming when I was five,' Leo explains, drying off after a two-hour morning session. 'My parents took me to the pool every weekend, but I didn't really take it seriously until I joined a club at ten.'

Leo’s routine is demanding. He wakes up at 4:30 a.m. to be in the water by 5:15 a.m. 'It’s tough, especially in winter when it's dark and cold outside,' he admits. 'But when you’re in the pool, you forget the time. You just focus on your strokes.' Despite the hard work, Leo insists he has a normal social life. 'People think athletes don't have time for friends, but I make sure I see my mates on Friday nights. It’s important to switch off.'

His biggest challenge so far was the National Youth Championships last year. 'I was so nervous before the final race,' he recalls. 'I almost pulled out, but my coach reminded me why I started. I ended up winning silver.' That medal changed his perspective. 'It wasn't just about the prize; it was about proving to myself that I could handle the pressure.'

Looking ahead, Leo has his sights set on the international stage. 'The dream is the Olympics, obviously. But for now, I’m focused on improving my technique. My coach says I’m strong, but my turns need work.' When asked if he has any advice for other young athletes, he is humble. 'Don't let the sport define who you are. Enjoy it, work hard, but remember to have fun. If you stop enjoying it, you’ll never reach your potential.'

questions.question: When did Leo start to treat swimming as a serious activity?
questions.explanation: Leo mentions he started at five but didn't take it seriously until he joined a club at ten.
options: a) When he was five years old.
b) After he won his first medal.
c) When he became a member of a swimming club.
d) When he started training in Manchester.

questions.question: How does Leo feel about his early morning training sessions?
questions.explanation: Leo acknowledges that the sessions are difficult, particularly due to the weather, but he finds focus once he is in the water.
options: a) He finds them easy because he is used to them.
b) He admits they are difficult but enjoys the focus they provide.
c) He wishes he could train later in the day.
d) He prefers training in the winter months.

questions.question: What does Leo say about his social life?
questions.explanation: Leo states that he makes time to see his friends on Friday nights to ensure he has a balance.
options: a) He has no time for friends because of his training.
b) He only sees his friends during school holidays.
c) He thinks it is impossible to be an athlete and have friends.
d) He believes it is important to take breaks from training to see friends.

questions.question: What was the most important result of winning a silver medal?
questions.explanation: Leo explains that the medal helped him prove to himself that he could manage the pressure of competition.
options: a) It gave him confidence that he could cope with pressure.
b) It meant he could stop training so hard.
c) It qualified him for the Olympic Games.
d) It made his parents very proud of him.

questions.question: What is Leo’s main piece of advice for young athletes?
questions.explanation: Leo emphasizes that enjoying the sport is key to reaching one's potential.
options: a) Always listen to what your coach says.
b) Focus entirely on your sport to succeed.
c) Keep enjoying the sport to reach your goals.
d) Try to win as many medals as possible.
